title: A polite harvester
description:
Write the component every integration eventually needs: something that reads **every** item of a paginated list from an API, however long it is and however badly the API behaves along the way. It follows `Link` headers, paces itself, retries what can be retried with backoff, honours `Retry-After`, removes duplicates, and refuses to loop forever.

```python
class HarvestError(Exception): ...

class Harvester:
    def __init__(self, transport, clock, sleep, rng, max_attempts=4, min_interval=0.2): ...
    def fetch_all(self, url): ...           # -> list of items
    requests                                # how many requests were sent
    retries                                 # how many of them were retries
```

`transport.send(method, url, headers)` returns `(status, headers, body)` (header names in any case, body as `bytes`) or raises `ConnectionError` or `TimeoutError`. `sleep(seconds)` waits; in the tests it moves the fake `clock` forward.

**Pages.** `fetch_all(url)` requests `url` with `GET` and the header `Accept: application/json`. A successful page has status 200 and a JSON object body with an `items` list. The next page's URL is the `rel="next"` link of the `Link` header (practice 3.01); with none, the harvest is complete. If a next URL was already requested during this harvest, raise `HarvestError` (a pagination loop).

**Items.** Return the items of all pages in order, **without duplicates**: an item is a duplicate if it has the same `id` as an earlier one; only the first is kept.

**Pacing.** Before every request (retries included), if fewer than `min_interval` seconds have passed since the previous request was sent, sleep for the difference first.

**Retries**, as in practice 3.03: an attempt that raised `ConnectionError` or `TimeoutError`, or returned 408, 429, 500, 502, 503 or 504, is retried until `max_attempts` attempts have been made **for that page**. Before a retry, sleep for the `Retry-After` header's seconds if it is a whole number in digits, otherwise `rng.uniform(0, min(8, 0.5 * 2 ** (n - 1)))` after attempt `n`. When the attempts run out, raise `HarvestError`.

**Other failures** raise `HarvestError` at once: any other status, a body that is not valid JSON, or a JSON body that is not an object with an `items` list.
hints: Split the work into three methods: one that sends a single request with pacing, one that gets one page with retries, and `fetch_all`, which loops over pages and collects items. Each is short and testable on its own.
Record the clock reading just before every send. The pacing wait is `min_interval - (now - last_sent)` when that is positive; retries go through the same send method, so they are paced too.
requirements: Every page is fetched exactly once when nothing fails, following `rel="next"` links until there are none.
Duplicate items are removed by `id`, keeping order.
Requests are never closer together than `min_interval`, retries included.
Retryable failures are retried with backoff, `Retry-After` wins over the computed delay, and the attempt limit is per page.
Loops, bad statuses and malformed pages stop the harvest with `HarvestError`.
